subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Six Types of Tea
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Six Types of Tea.

hook.text: Tea experts classify all true tea into six types based on processing: white, green, yellow, oolong, black, dark.

buildup.text: White is barely processed. Green is heated early. Yellow is lightly fermented under a damp cloth.

discovery.text: Oolong is partially oxidized (15–85%). Black is fully oxidized. Dark tea (like pu-erh) is microbially aged.

twist.text: Yellow tea is the rarest. The extra step of 'smothering' creates a smooth, mellow flavor few people ever taste.

climax.text: Each type contains thousands of individual teas—varieties within varieties, shaped by region and technique.

punchline.text: Six types, thousands of teas. One plant did all that.

quiz.question: What makes pu-erh different from other tea types?
